title: Mobile Friendly Test by Google Is Gone — Test Here

body:
## What happened to Google's Mobile-Friendly Test?

Google removed the Mobile-Friendly Test, its API and the Mobile Usability report in December 2023, and deleted mentions of them from its documentation ([Search Central updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates)). This test runs on [Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview), Google's open-source auditing engine, through the PageSpeed Insights API.

The reason it went away matters: mobile-friendliness didn't stop mattering, it became the default. Google now indexes and ranks [the mobile version of your pages](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/mobile/mobile-sites-mobile-first-indexing), crawled with Googlebot Smartphone.

## Mobile Friendly Test: Screenshot, Viewport and Tap Targets

The test combines a live fetch with a mobile Lighthouse run:

| Check | Fails when |
|---|---|
| Viewport meta tag | Missing, so phones render a shrunken desktop page |
| Fixed-width elements | Inline widths of 1000px or more |
| Tap targets | Buttons and links too small or too close together |
| Legible font sizes | Too much text below a readable size |
| Content fits the screen | The page scrolls sideways |
| Googlebot Smartphone request | The page fails for both a phone browser and Googlebot |

You also get the mobile screenshot Lighthouse captured, so you can see what a phone actually rendered.

## Mobile Friendly Tester: What a Pass Actually Means

A pass means the page works on a phone: it scales, it's readable and it's tappable. It doesn't mean it's fast. Speed on mobile is measured separately by Core Web Vitals, where many sites that look fine on a phone still fail.

The basics are nearly universal now: in our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 99% set a viewport tag. The failures we see more often are content that only appears on desktop — and Google says the mobile and desktop versions should carry the same content so both can rank.

## What should I fix first?

The viewport tag and horizontal scrolling, because they break the whole page; then tap targets and font sizes. Make sure your mobile version has the same main content, structured data and metadata as desktop.

Then check speed with the [Core Web Vitals test](/tools/core-web-vitals-test), and confirm what Googlebot Smartphone receives with the [Googlebot simulator](/tools/googlebot-simulator).

faqs.q: Is the Google Mobile-Friendly Test still available?
faqs.a: No. Google retired the Mobile-Friendly Test, its API and the Mobile Usability report in December 2023 and pointed site owners to Lighthouse, which powers this test.
Google indexes and ranks the mobile version of pages, so a page that is broken on phones is effectively broken for Google. Speed and usability on mobile also feed page experience.

faqs.q: Why does the test take longer than other tools?
faqs.a: It runs a full Lighthouse audit on an emulated phone through Google's PageSpeed Insights API, which loads and renders the page. That usually takes 20 to 40 seconds.
